message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for my boyfriend to always walk ahead of me when we're out together. I've mentioned this to him before, and he says it's just because he has longer strides because he's taller. But every time we walk somewhere, especially in new places like when we went on vacation, I end up struggling to keep up. I feel like I'm not his girlfriend when he doesn't walk beside me. I've tried wearing flats sometimes, but even then, it's hard to keep up, especially when I'm in heels half the time. I just want to walk alongside him, hold hands, and have a conversation without straining to hear him or keep up. I finally blew up at him during our vacation, and now I'm wondering if I'm overreacting or if he really can't help it. Is this a big deal, or should I just let it go? First, I need to understand why walking side by side is important to me. It seems like it's about feeling connected and valued in the relationship. When he walks ahead, I feel disconnected and like I'm not being considered. It's not just about the physical effort of keeping up; it's more about the emotional impact of feeling left behind. On the other hand, my boyfriend says he can't help walking faster because of his longer strides. Maybe he doesn't realize how much it affects me emotionally. It's possible that he doesn't intend to make me feel this way; he might just be focused on getting to our destination quickly. I should consider whether there's a middle ground. Maybe we can compromise on how we walk together. For example, he could adjust his pace slightly to match mine, or we could take breaks if we're walking a long distance. It might also help to have a conversation about why this is important to me and see if we can find a solution that works for both of us. I also need to reflect on whether this issue is worth getting upset over. Relationships have many ups and downs, and sometimes small things can feel like big issues. However, if this is consistently causing me distress and affecting our connection, it might be worth addressing to improve our relationship. In the end, communication seems key here. I should express my feelings calmly and see if we can find a way to walk together that makes both of us feel good about our time spent together.
